versions.changelog:
**Major update: adds structured Zotero integration and attachment relocation, new documentation, and refines workflows.**

- Introduced extensive Zotero sync, allocation, healing, and relocation workflows; added corresponding CLI commands and YAML-driven processes.
- Added 25 new files, including code modules for BM25 search, capabilities, claims management, transaction handling, dataset sanitization, and detailed Zotero client utilities.
- Added rich documentation: skill architecture/performance, Zotero integration, relocation steps, and YAML workflow examples.
- Expanded and clarified workflows in SKILL.md for ingest, query, linking, and Zotero-backed management; documented relocation root configuration and secure/authorized writeback.
- Removed deprecated commands module and old skill card to streamline codebase and documentation.
- Improved CLI guidance, with new dry-run, allocation, healing, ingest-verification, and writeback strategies for advanced agent/Zotero operation.

LLM-Wiki 1.5.2

- Added project documentation and packaging guides, including templates and config examples.
- Introduced new source files for command initialization and PDF/image processing.
- Expanded `templates/` with Markdown page templates, agent protocol, config, and readme files.
- Removed deprecated `skill-card.md`.
- Updated skill manifest to include version number and clarified the agent audience in the description.

- Removed all compiled Python cache files from the repository to clean up versioned files.
- No feature or documentation changes; operational behavior and user protocols remain unchanged.

Version 1.5.0 of 041-llm-wiki introduces new linting and ingest safeguards.

- Added "depth lint" tools for measuring wiki page knowledge depth; included `src/llm_wiki/depth_lint.py` and compiled helpers.
- Enhanced ingest workflow: require source mapping, allocation, and explicit omission reasoning for better coverage and auditability.
- Improved integration guidance for Zotero and agent-MCP workflows; new checks on tool availability and operation verification.
- Clarified that "Shallow Pages" reported by lint are warnings only, not errors; added rules for exemption handling.
- Added a sample configuration file (`config.yaml.example`) and a Zotero source script.
- Removed the old `skill-card.md`.

- The skill-card.md file was removed.
- SKILL.md was replaced with a concise operational description, focusing on procedures, workflows, and verification steps for managing an llm-wiki knowledge base.
- Details on capabilities, dependencies, and CLI installation were removed from SKILL.md.
- The new SKILL.md emphasizes the use of agent-bridge.py for all algorithmic tasks and provides streamlined guidelines for ingest, query, and linking workflows.
- Zotero integration guidance and source fetch safety checks are now included directly in SKILL.md.

llm-wiki 1.4.1

- Added extraction and preservation of temporal metadata (published, collected, ingested dates, and precision) for sources during ingest.
- Enhanced guidance for agents: maintain clear distinction between wiki maintenance dates and original source/work dates in frontmatter and content.
- Introduced recommended visible time anchor formatting for timelines and summaries using Markdown.
- Lint workflow updated: dead link check now verifies wiki file stems; added checks for empty pages, duplicate titles, and non-canonical links.
- New documentation and utility scripts added; removed obsolete expert page template.

Version 1.4.0

- Introduced agent-bridge interface (`scripts/agent-bridge.py`) as a unified entry point for all automation and agent interactions.
- Added dedicated agent logging module (`src/llm_wiki/agent_logger.py`) for improved traceability and debugging.
- Updated SKILL definition to reference the new agent-bridge script in entry points, workflows, and CLI documentation.
- Revised ingest, link, and relink function workflows to use the agent-bridge tool for discovery, merging, and batch operations.
- Enhanced documentation to distinguish between protocol mode, agent bridge usage, and legacy CLI.

# llm-wiki v1.1.4 Changelog

- Added a new file: `docs/README.cn.md` (Chinese README).
- No changes to code or functionality; documentation improvement only.

Version 1.3.0 introduces relationship linking and merging capabilities for wiki pages.

- Added new CLI commands and core functions for dynamic linking (`link`) and batch relationship discovery (`relink`) between wiki pages.
- Introduced `src/llm_wiki/linker.py` and `src/llm_wiki/merge.py` modules to support relationship discovery and merge strategies.
- Enhanced `ingest` workflow to automatically suggest and update page relationships, with options for light or deep linking.
- Updated function documentation to reflect new workflows, triggers, and relationship management steps.
- Increased version number to 1.3.0 to reflect these significant new knowledge graph and linking features.

- Added `log.md` for timeline/changelog tracking.
- Added `wiki/index.md` as a structured index entry point.
- Updated and reorganized dependency list to include `pymupdf`, `numpy`, `httpx`, `openai`, and `mcp` for enhanced PDF and embedding support.
- Clarified and expanded CLI and installation instructions in documentation.
- Updated security notes about fallback PDF handling in the README.
- Improved documentation across AGENTS.md, ROADMAP.md, and new file handling details.

- Introduced stub page creation for any new [[Dead Link]] encountered during content ingestion.
- Added new source files: config.py, embeddings.py, and retrieval.py to enhance functionality.
- Removed redundant files: log.md and wiki/index.md as part of project restructuring.

- Updated the repository URL in metadata from "https://github.com/yourname/llm-wiki" to "https://github.com/Nemo4110/llm-wiki.git".
- No functional, interface, or code changes were made.

No changes detected in this version.

- Version bumped to 1.0.2, but no code or documentation changes from previous release.
- All features, structure, and instructions remain unchanged.

Version 1.0.1

- Added `src/llm_wiki/__main__.py` to support direct CLI invocation via `python -m src.llm_wiki`.
- Expanded documentation in SKILL.md to include a detailed CLI reference and installation notes.
- Added security warnings and dependency version requirements for PDF processing libraries.
- No changes to core functions or protocol—this is a documentation and usability update.

Initial release of llm-wiki skill — cumulative knowledge management for AI agents.

- Implements Karpathy’s llm-wiki pattern for managing and querying knowledge.
- Supports ingestion of source material, wiki querying, and lint/health checks.
- Compatible with Claude Code, OpenClaw, and generic LLM-agent platforms.
- Offers both protocol (no dependencies) and CLI (Python + click/pyyaml) modes.
- Provides clear separation of sources, wiki content, scripts, and examples.
- Detailed installation options and accessible documentation included.
